verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_filter_blocks_xss: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Functions have docstrings and numbered comments, but the core tokenising logic is full of single-letter names (`p`, `q`, `n`, `c`, `i`) in `clean_tag_attributes`, `find_tag_closing_bracket` and `filter_html_once`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `filter_html_once` is about 130 lines (over the 100-line cap) and nests branches deeply. The same detection regex `<\s*script\b|on[a-zA-Z]+\s*=|javascript\s*:` is copied 4 times. The policy is not kept in named constants, and the script and style handling is duplicated.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Reads and writes with explicit encoding/newline and checks the file exists, but the base64 check uses `except Exception: pass`. It also has magic numbers such as `range(10)` and slice offsets like `i += 5` / `+ 9`.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: No element deny-list: `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, `<base>`, `<math>` and `<template>` all pass through. `data:text/html` is only blocked if it matches a regex, and null-byte-split `<script>` tags are not handled. The hidden test_filter_blocks_xss failed.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: Slices out only the dangerous attributes and script elements, keeping original quoting, attribute order, whitespace and benign attributes (seen in log [59] output). The hidden clean-doc test also failed, probably because it expects re-serialised output.
